Alternatively to the X9.62 encoding of ecdsa signatures
ASN.1 and is already supported by the kernel
encoding called P1363.  It stores r and s as the concatenation of two
big endian
column2: unsigned integers.  The name originates from IEEE P1363.

column1: Add a P1363 template in support of the forthcoming SPDM library
(Security Protocol and Data Model) for PCI device authentication.
P1363 is prescribed by SPDM 1.2.1 margin no 44:
""For ECDSA signatures
the concatenation of r and s.  The size of r shall be the size of
the selected curve.  Likewise
column2: the size of s shall be the size of

column1: the selected curve.  See BaseAsymAlgo in NEGOTIATE_ALGORITHMS for
the size of r and s.  The byte order for r and s shall be in big
endian order.  When placing ECDSA signatures into an SPDM signature
field
column2: r shall come first followed by s.""
